newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics adds VDOnet's video features.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics adds VDOnet's video features.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp on Friday said it has licensed VDOnet Corp 's video communications software to beef up its Bigpicture package, a system for transferring video over the Internet.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed.
VDOnet's s VDOPhone software for video communications and VDOLive software for Internet video broadcasting will be integrated into Bigpicture's package of VideoFun software.

The Bigpicture system, which includes a video camera, image capturing card, video editing software and modem, will allow consumers to make video telephone calls and send video e-mail, the company said. It is set for release in December.

VDOLive allows Web users to eliminate the need to download a file and wait minutes before even a short video clip is ready for viewing. VDOPhone allows anyone with a modem and a phone line to have full-color motion video conversations over the Internet or over regular phone lines, the company said.

"We have entered into a new era when transmitting data is not enough to get the full benefit from communications," said Michael Seedman, vice president of U.S. Robotics' Personal Communications Division. "VDOnet's video solutions are powerful in bringing broadcasting and video conferencing capabilities to the Internet."

The Internet video package comes as U.S. Robotics gears up for the first quarter 1997 introduction of its 56 thousand bit-per-second (kbps) modems, which will transfer data through telephone lines at twice the speed of the current standard.
Competing firms like Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc, Cardinal Technologies Inc and Rockwell International Corp also expected to ship versions of the faster modems early in 1997.
U.S. Robotics stock rose 1-3/8 to 71-5/8 in early afternoon trade.
